proposals.before: The Xia dynasty rose through Tushan, but Jie was banished because of Moyi.
proposals.after: The Xia dynasty rose through Tushan, but Jie was banished because of Moxi.
proposals.reason: Literal English renders 末喜 as Moyi; the established form matching the idiomatic line is Moxi.

proposals.before: Empress Lü's eldest daughter became the wife of Marquis Xuanping Zhang Ao, and Ao's daughter became Empress Xiaohui.
proposals.after: Empress Lü's eldest daughter became the wife of Marquis Xuanping Zhang Ao, and Ao's daughter became the empress of Emperor Xiaohui.
proposals.reason: 孝惠皇后 is the empress of Emperor Xiaohui, not a woman named Xiaohui.

proposals.before: Because of their close kinship, Empress Lü desired that the empress bear children by any means necessary. In the end, she bore no children, so she fraudulently took a son from one of the palace women and claimed him as her own.
proposals.after: Because of their close kinship, Empress Lü desired that the empress bear children by any means necessary. In the end the empress bore no children, so Empress Lü fraudulently took a son from one of the palace women and claimed him as the empress's own.
proposals.reason: 終無子 refers to the young empress, while 詐取 is Empress Lü's act; the literal English collapses both to a single she.

proposals.before: Therefore, she honored her maternal relatives, enfeoffed the various Lü clansmen as kings to serve as supporters, and made Lü Lü's daughter the consort of the young emperor, wishing to firmly establish and strengthen their family foundation. However, it was of no avail.
proposals.after: Therefore, she honored her maternal relatives, enfeoffed the various Lü clansmen as kings to serve as supporters, and made Lü Lu's daughter the consort of the young emperor, wishing to firmly establish and strengthen their family foundation. However, it was of no avail.
proposals.reason: 呂祿 is Lü Lu, not Lü Lü.

proposals.before: Lü Lü and Lü Chan and the others, fearing execution, plotted rebellion.
proposals.after: Lü Lu and Lü Chan and the others, fearing execution, plotted rebellion.
proposals.reason: 祿 is Lü Lu; Lü Lü is a transcription error.

proposals.before: Only Empress Xiaohui was left dwelling in the Northern Palace.
proposals.after: Only Emperor Xiaohui's empress was left dwelling in the Northern Palace.
proposals.reason: 孝惠皇后 is Emperor Xiaohui's empress, not Empress Xiaohui.

proposals.before: Empress Bo's father was from Wu, surnamed Bo. During the Qin dynasty, he had relations with Wei Fu, a woman from the clan of the former King of Wei, and she bore Empress Bo. Bo An died in Shanyin and was buried there.
proposals.after: Empress Bo's father was from Wu, surnamed Bo. During the Qin dynasty, he had relations with Wei Ao, a woman from the clan of the former King of Wei, and she bore Empress Bo. Bo An died in Shanyin and was buried there.
proposals.reason: 魏媼 is Wei Ao (old woman/matron), not Wei Fu.

proposals.before: Empress Dowager Bo outlived Emperor Wen by two years, dying in the second year before Emperor Jing's reign, and was buried at Nanling.
proposals.after: Empress Dowager Bo outlived Emperor Wen by two years, dying in the second year of Emperor Jing's former era, and was buried at Nanling.
proposals.reason: 孝景帝前二年 is Jing's former-era year 2 (155 BC), not a year before Jing's reign; 後文帝二年 already states she died two years after Wen.

proposals.before: The following year, her youngest son Wu was established as King of Dai, but later moved to Liang, becoming King Xiaoxiao of Liang.
proposals.after: The following year, her youngest son Wu was established as King of Dai, but later moved to Liang, becoming King Xiao of Liang.
proposals.reason: 梁孝王 is King Xiao of Liang; Xiaoxiao doubles the 孝 element and is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Empress Dou's mother died early and was buried in Guanjin.
proposals.after: Empress Dou's parents died early and were buried in Guanjin.
proposals.reason: 親蚤卒 refers to both parents (father and mother), matching the following posthumous honors of father and mother.

proposals.before: The Marquis of Jiang and General Guan Ying and others said: "If we are to survive, our fate for the moment hangs on these two men.
proposals.after: The Marquis of Jiang and General Guan and others said: "If we are to survive, our fate for the moment hangs on these two men.
proposals.reason: Chinese 灌將軍 does not supply the given name Ying; the idiomatic rendering correctly keeps General Guan.

proposals.before: Zang Er's eldest daughter married into the Jin family as Jin Wangsun's wife, and already bore a daughter, but Zang Er divined for them and said both daughters would be noble.
proposals.after: Zang Er's eldest daughter married into the Jin family as Jin Wangsun's wife, and already bore a daughter, but Zang Er consulted a diviner, who declared that both daughters would be noble.
proposals.reason: The 曰 after 卜筮之 reports the diviner's verdict; the literal wrongly makes Zang Er herself the speaker of the prophecy.

proposals.before: Therefore, wishing to make the two daughters exceptional, she took them from the Jin family.
proposals.after: Therefore, wishing to make the two daughters exceptional, she took the elder back from the Jin family.
proposals.reason: 奪金氏 refers to reclaiming the daughter married into the Jin family, not both daughters.

proposals.before: When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Bo made a Bo family daughter his consort.
proposals.after: When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo made a Bo family daughter his consort.
proposals.reason: 薄太后 is Empress Dowager Bo, not Empress Bo.

proposals.before: When Empress Bo passed away, Empress Bo was deposed.
proposals.after: When Empress Dowager Bo passed away, Empress Bo was deposed.
proposals.reason: 崩 is 薄太后; 廢薄皇后 is a different person.

proposals.before: The eldest princess daily praised the beauty of Lady Wang's son, and Emperor Jing also considered him worthy, moreover there was the previous dream of the sun as an omen, so his plans were not yet decided.
proposals.after: The eldest princess daily praised the excellence of Lady Wang's son, and Emperor Jing also considered him worthy; moreover there was the previous dream of the sun as an omen, so his plans were not yet decided.
proposals.reason: 之美 paired with 賢之 denotes worth, not physical beauty.

proposals.before: As for Empress Wei's sister Wei Shao'er, she bore a son named Huo Qubing, who for his military exploits was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun and held the title of General of Swift Cavalry.
proposals.after: As for Empress Wei's so-called sister Wei Shao'er, she bore a son named Huo Qubing, who for his military exploits was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun and held the title of General of Swift Cavalry.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 所謂姊 marks the sisterhood as qualified or reported, which the idiomatic English drops.

proposals.before: As for Empress Wei's so-called sister Wei Shaorer, Shaorer bore a son Huo Qubing, who for military merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanju, and styled General Champion.
proposals.after: As for Empress Wei's so-called sister Wei Shao'er, Shao'er bore a son Huo Qubing, who for military merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun, and styled General of Swift Cavalry.
proposals.reason: 冠軍侯 is Guanjun, not Guanju; 驃騎將軍 is General of Swift Cavalry, not General Champion; Shaorer should match Shao'er.

proposals.before: Emperor Wu presented wine and toasted her longevity, bestowed ten million cash, three hundred slaves and maids, one hundred qing of public fields, and an armored residence, to grant to his sister.
proposals.after: Emperor Wu presented wine and toasted her longevity, bestowed ten million cash, three hundred slaves and maids, one hundred qing of public fields, and a first-class mansion, to grant to his sister.
proposals.reason: 甲第 is a grand first-rank residence, not an armored residence.

proposals.before: The son was styled Xiuchengzi Zhong, the daughter became queen consort to various feudal kings.
proposals.after: The son was styled Xiuchengzi Zhong, and the daughter became queen consort to a feudal king.
proposals.reason: 諸侯王王后 denotes queen to a feudal king, not queens to various kings.

proposals.before: Lady Xing was styled Jiao'e, people called her "Jiao He."
proposals.after: Lady Xing was styled Jing'e; people called her "Jing He."
proposals.reason: 娙娥/娙何 are Jing'e/Jing He, matching the idiomatic rendering; Jiao is a wrong reading.

proposals.before: Therefore, all who bore sons for Emperor Wu, regardless of male or female children, their mothers without exception were reproached to death—can this be said not to be worthy and sage-like!
proposals.after: Therefore, of all who bore children for Emperor Wu, whether the child was male or female, their mothers without exception were reproached to death—can this be said not to be worthy and sage-like!
proposals.reason: 生子者，無男女 means those who bore Wu's children of either sex, not only sons; the literal rendering 'bore sons' then 'regardless of male or female children' is internally inconsistent.

proposals.before: She replied, "Judging by her figure, features, and bearing, she is not beautiful enough to captivate a sovereign."
proposals.after: She replied, "Judging by her figure, features, and bearing, they are not adequate to a sovereign."
proposals.reason: 不足以當人主 describes insufficiency to match or befit a ruler, not specifically a failure to captivate; the idiomatic version invents the captivation sense.

decisions.reason: 末喜 is the consort Moxi; Moyi misreads 喜 and does not match the established form used in the idiomatic line.
孝惠皇后 names Zhang Ao's daughter as the empress of Emperor Xiaohui, not a woman whose name is Xiaohui.
欲其生子 and 終無子 refer to the young empress, while 詐取…為子 is Empress Dowager Lü's fraud; the original she collapses agent and patient.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 欲其生子萬方，終無子，詐取後宮人子為子

decisions.reason: 呂祿 is Lü Lu; Lü Lü wrongly repeats the surname as the given name.
祿 is the given name Lu of Lü Lu, continued from 呂祿 in s0023; Lü Lü is a transcription error.
孝惠皇后 is Emperor Xiaohui's empress, the same woman as in s0020, not an empress named Xiaohui.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唯獨置孝惠皇后居北宮

decisions.after: Empress Dowager Bo's father was from Wu, surnamed Bo. During the Qin dynasty, he had relations with Wei Ao, a woman from the clan of the former King of Wei, and she bore Bo Ji. Bo An died in Shanyin and was buried there.
decisions.reason: 魏媼 is Wei Ao, not Wei Fu, but the proposed after still renders 薄太后 as Empress Bo and 生薄姬 as bearing Empress Bo.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 薄太后，父吳人，姓薄氏，秦時與故魏王宗家女魏媼通，生薄姬

decisions.reason: 孝景帝前二年 is year 2 of Jing's former era, already two years after Wen (後文帝二年), not a year before Jing's reign.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 薄太后後文帝二年，以孝景帝前二年崩

decisions.reason: 梁孝王 is King Xiao of Liang; Xiaoxiao invents a doubled 孝 that is not in the Chinese.
親蚤卒 is the early death of both parents, as the next sentence's separate honors of 父 and 母 confirm; mother alone undertranslates 親.
灌將軍 supplies only the surname and office; Ying is not in this sentence and should not appear in the literal English.
卜筮之，曰 introduces the oracle's verdict after Zang Er had a divination performed; the original makes Zang Er herself utter the prophecy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 而臧兒卜筮之，曰兩女皆當貴

decisions.reason: 奪金氏 reclaims the daughter who had married into the Jin family; 兩女 is the motive, not the object taken, and s0107 continues with a single 之.
薄太后 is Empress Dowager Bo, distinct from the 薄氏女 later made 薄皇后 in s0114.
薄太后崩 and 廢薄皇后 name two different women; the original makes the same Empress Bo both die and be deposed.
譽王夫人男之美 is paired with 景帝亦賢之 in a succession debate, so 美 is excellence or worth, not physical beauty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 長公主日譽王夫人男之美，景帝亦賢之

decisions.reason: 所謂姊 qualifies the sisterhood as reported or so-called; omitting 所謂 is a semantic loss, not a stylistic trim.
衛少兒 is Shao'er, 冠軍侯 is Marquis of Guanjun, and 驃騎將軍 is General of Swift Cavalry; Guanju, Shaorer, and General Champion are inaccurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 少兒生子霍去病，以軍功封冠軍侯，號驃騎將軍

decisions.reason: 甲第 is a first-rank mansion, not an armored residence.
諸侯王王后 is the status of queen to a feudal king; various kings overreads 諸侯王 as multiple husbands.
娙娥 and 娙何 are Jing'e and Jing He in this chapter's established rendering; Jiao is the wrong reading of 娙.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 邢夫人號娙娥，眾人謂之「娙何」

decisions.reason: 為武帝生子者，無男女 means every woman who bore Wu a child of either sex; bore sons contradicts 無男女.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 諸為武帝生子者，無男女，其母無不譴死

decisions.after: She replied, "Judging by her figure, features, and bearing, she is not fit to match a sovereign."
decisions.reason: 不足以當人主 is failure to match or befit a ruler, not failure to captivate, but the proposed they are not adequate to a sovereign is awkward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 視其身貌形狀，不足以當人主矣

value.assessment: bearing sufficient to captivate a sovereign
bearing sufficient to match a sovereign

claimRevisions.reason: Lady Yin's 不足以當人主 judges whether the woman's appearance befits a ruler, not whether it captivates him; the extracted assessment copied the bad idiomatic rendering.
